- If sentiment is positive (≥0.5) and forecast is significantly above true outcome, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.25) and forecast is below true outcome, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- When true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a spike, model often overshoots downward — adjust forecast to be 1–2% less negative than model.  
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per day from forecast until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral (0.00) and forecast is >10% above true, reduce forecast by 10–15% to avoid overfitting recent trends.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.5 spikes, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast by 5–8% for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome is below 65 and forecast is above 70, reduce forecast by 10–15% to avoid overestimating recovery.  
- If forecast is below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, model may be underestimating — increase forecast by 2–5% to avoid underreaction.
